input.title: 48-vertex connected cubic counterexample to independent domination versus minimum maximal matching
input.status: unrefereed candidate; bundled proof tree verified

routes.title: Find and independently check an explicit transversal

source.location: Proposition 6; finite assignment enumeration supplied by this pilot

routes.basis: Enumerate all 2^|M| assignments, reconstruct each first satisfying selection, then check domination from the original edges without using the clauses.
routes.limit: At most 20 matching edges and 1,048,576 assignments. An exhausted user budget is inconclusive. No-transversal excludes only this restricted route.

routes.title: Prior-art stop: the order-48 inequality is already covered
routes.basis: The cited preprint states gamma <= gamma_e for cubic graphs of order at most 48, using a minimum unsatisfiable bounded-occurrence CNF classification.
routes.limit: Imported preprint and classification, not reverified here. Use this as a duplicate-research warning; the direct finite witness removes the imported classification from the pilot's conclusion.

routes.title: Reformulate domination as endpoint-transversal SAT
routes.basis: One Boolean variable selects an endpoint of each matching edge. A clause for every unmatched vertex requires a neighbour to be selected. Vertices adjacent to both endpoints of one edge give tautologies. Matched vertices are automatically dominated.
routes.limit: SAT is equivalent to a dominating transversal of this matching, not to an arbitrary dominating set. The implemented equivalence also handles non-cubic finite simple graphs.

routes.title: Certify the supplied matching is minimum
routes.basis: A maximal matching edge-dominates all edges. Each edge covers at most 2 Delta - 1 edges; ceiling(m/(2 Delta - 1)) is a lower bound. Equality with a checked witness establishes minimality.
routes.limit: Works when this elementary lower bound is attained. Otherwise minimality remains unknown, not false.

routes.title: Chain the checked witness into an ordinary-domination upper bound

source.location: Section 1: definition of domination; Section 4: witness upper bound

routes.basis: Every vertex is either in the selected set or adjacent to it, so gamma(G) is at most the witness size.
routes.limit: An upper bound is not an exact minimum. No lower bound is inferred from failure of a restricted search.

routes.title: Independent domination transfers only an upper bound
routes.basis: Every independent dominating set is dominating: gamma <= i. A lower bound on i is NOT a lower bound on gamma.
routes.limit: Knowing i=16 does not prove gamma>=16. This invalid transfer is deliberately absent from the rule library.

routes.title: Decide that this graph is not an ordinary-domination counterexample
routes.basis: Combine a graph-checked dominating set of size at most |M| with a checked minimum maximal matching M. This proves gamma(G) <= gamma_e(G) for this exact graph.
routes.limit: No universal statement about regular graphs; the two graph objects and parameter meanings must be identical.
